title: Crop legacies as genetic targets for sustainable farming systems.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: There are no data files to open. Europe PMC lists this as pubType 'Review', isOpenAccess=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, hasDbCrossReferences=N, no text-mined accessions and no PMCID, so no full text or supplement is retrievable. scripts/paper_context.py returned empty accession, NCBI-link and Zenodo/Dryad searches. I fetched the publisher landing page (387 KB of HTML) and grepped it: zero hits for 'Data availability', 'Supplementary information', 'Source data', Zenodo, figshare, Dryad or GitHub, and 10 hits for 'Perspective' (the article type). Crossref confirms a 9-page article (pages 2448-2456) with 59 references and no abstract deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the science comes from the abstract alone: the claim that crop legacy effects on soil nutrients, water, structure and microbial communities vary heritably within major crop species and could be bred for. A web search surfaced a press release and a companion bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2025.11.03.686422, 'The potential to breed for genetic legacy effects in sustainable farming systems') describing a mung bean to wheat rotation experiment; I could not retrieve that preprint (HTTP 429), so I verified none of its contents and it is a different paper in any case.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. This is a Perspective (opinion/review) article in Nature Genetics. It reports no primary measurements, has no supplementary files, no data availability statement, no repository accession and no source data, and the text itself is paywalled. There is literally nothing to download.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessed beyond A1: with no table of any kind, there is no column, no label and no key. The quantity the paper is about (next-crop yield as a function of the previous crop's genotype) would have to be assembled from other people's field trials.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessed; no files exist. Genotype data for any crop line discussed is not provided or referenced by accession.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessed; no measurements are reported in a machine-readable form.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not assessed; zero rows available. I did not see any row count and am recording null rather than guessing.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially true and meaningless: there is no data to load.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable; there is no download to compare the paper against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable; no label exists. The paper argues that legacy effects should become breeding targets, but supplies no measured legacy-effect values.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper is a forward-looking Perspective with no dataset attached, so nothing can be trained, tested or even counted.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the genetics of one crop variety to predict how well the next crop in the rotation grows.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would need, for each field plot, the identity or genetic markers of the crop variety grown in season one plus soil measurements it left behind. This paper supplies none of these, so the example count is unknown (zero available here).
plain_idea.predict: The yield of the following crop in the same plot, measured by harvest weighing in a field trial. No such measurements are provided by this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Plant breeders currently select varieties on their own yield alone; if a variety's effect on the next crop were predictable from its genetics, breeding programmes could select for whole rotations and farmers could cut fertiliser use. The idea is attractive, but this particular article contributes argument rather than data.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: predict the yield of crop B from the genotype of the crop A variety grown in the same plot the previous season (a 'legacy effect' prediction). The idea is sound and genuinely unmodelled, but it cannot be built from this article, which contains no measurements. A real version would need multi-year, multi-genotype rotation trials with plot-level yields and genotype data, which exist in breeding-programme archives but are not released here.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful because there is no data; all fields left null rather than invented.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Grep the publisher page for 'Data availability' and 'Supplementary'. Both return zero hits, which killed the candidate in one command.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright: this is a paywalled Nature Genetics Perspective (Europe PMC pubType 'Review', hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no PMCID, no accessions, no Zenodo/Dryad hit, and no 'Data availability' or 'Supplementary' string anywhere on the publisher page). It proposes that crop legacy effects on the following season's crop should become breeding targets, but reports no measurements of its own, so there is no table, no label and no row to count. Per the checklist I stopped at the first failed killer and did not run the C2 existing-models audit. Worth noting for the pipeline, not for this paper: the same Queensland group has a companion bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2025.11.03.686422) that appears to describe an actual mung bean to wheat rotation experiment; I could not retrieve it (HTTP 429) and verified nothing about it, but it, not this Perspective, would be the thing to screen if legacy-effect prediction is of interest.
